This is a claim petition u/s 166 of M.V. Act filed by the petitioner seeking compensation in respect of the injuries sustained by him in a road accident involving vehicle i.e. Truck bearing registration no. HR69A 8665.

As per the claim petition as well as documents filed on record, on 20.01.2020, the petitioner was going from Delhi to Pune while driving his Eicher Truck no. DL1LT2063 and at about 11 AM, when he reached at Village Chhapli Ghata within the jurisdiction of PS Dewair, suddenly, a vehicle i.e. Truck bearing registration no. HR-69A-8665 (hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle') being driven by respondent no. 1 Asmoon in a rash and negligent manner, came from opposite side and hit against the vehicle of petitioner, due to which, the petitioner suffered grievous injuries on his right leg.

It is further stated that initially, the injured was taken to Community Health Center, Deogarh, District Alwar, Rajasthan vide registration no. 302; that thereafter, he started getting himself medically treated from Dr. Sanjay Multi Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Bahadurgarh,
Haryana.

ISSUE No.1 1.

Whether the petitioner Aliyas suffered injuries in a vehicular accident that took place on 20.01.2020 at about 11 AM at Village Chhapli Ghata, PS Dewair, Rajasthan involving truck bearing registration no. HR69A8665 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no.1/Asmoon in a rash and negligent manner, owned by respondent no.2 Lal Bahadur and insured with United India Insurance Company Limited? OPP 9.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the SACHIN

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

ISSUE No.2 2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
16.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION
OF COMPENSATION
17. The scope of compensation in injury cases has been SACHIN

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.
Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv)
inconvenience, discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
18. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.05.03 16:33:06 +0530 MACT No.
577/2021 Date of Award: 03.05.2025 4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.05.03 16:33:14 +0530 MACT No. 577/2021 Date of Award: 03.05.2025 (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.

Aliyas vs Asmoon And Ors on 3 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32291091/
6 (iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general  damages)
 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b),
(iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

sentences.text: In order to deal with the aforesaid contention raised on behalf of the insurance company, it is relevant to refer the documents/reports available on record.

In the certified copy of charge sheet,
which is part of Ex.PW1/7 (colly), it has been mentioned by the IO that he obtained the copy of the driver's license from the owner of truck bearing no. HR69A 8665 (offending vehicle herein).

Further, certified copy of complete challan which is Ex.PW1/7 filed by the petitioner also consist of the copy of notice U/s 134 M.V. Act which was given by the IO to the Asmoon (respondent no.1 herein) driver of the offending vehicle and its reply given by him, wherein driver has stated inter alia that he was driving the truck no. HR69A 8665 at the time of accident and he furnished the copy of his driving license to the IO.
The aforesaid document/report remained undisputed on the part of the insurance company.

It clearly shows that as per the reply of driver of the offending vehicle (respondent no.1) to the notice U/s 134 M.V. Act served upon him by the IO, he has furnished the copy of his driving license to the IO.

Meaning thereby the respondent no.1 was having a driving license at the time of accident, which is further substantiated by the fact that IO has not invoked Section 3/181 M.V. Act in the charge-sheet filed by him against the accused(respondent no.1 herein).
In view of the aforesaid discussion and material available on record, the aforesaid plea of the insurance company is not found sustainable.

Since, it is an admitted case of the respondent No. 3 /
Insurance Company that the aforesaid vehicle No. HR69A 8665 (offending vehicle) was duly insured with it, therefore, respondent No. 3 / Insurance Co. is liable to pay the amount of compensation to the petitioner / claimant.
Issue no. 2 is decided accordingly.

This is a claim petition u/s 166 of M.V. Act filed by the petitioner seeking compensation in respect of the injuries sustained by him in a road accident involving vehicle i.e. Truck bearing registration no. HR69A 8665.
As per the claim petition as well as documents filed on record, on 20.01.2020, the petitioner was going from Delhi to Pune while driving his Eicher Truck no. DL1LT2063 and at about 11 AM, when he reached at Village Chhapli Ghata within the jurisdiction of PS Dewair, suddenly, a vehicle i.e. Truck bearing registration no. HR-69A-8665 (hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle') being driven by respondent no. 1 Asmoon in a rash and negligent manner, came from opposite side and hit against the vehicle of petitioner, due to which, the petitioner suffered grievous injuries on his right leg.
It is further stated that initially, the injured was taken to Community Health Center, Deogarh, District Alwar, Rajasthan vide registration no. 302; that thereafter, he started getting himself medically treated from Dr. Sanjay Multi Speciality Hospital Pvt. Ltd., Bahadurgarh,
Haryana.
It is further stated that FIR No. 22/2020 dated 03.03.2020, PS Dewair, District Alwar U/s 279/337/338 IPC pertaining to the accident was registered.
2. As per the claim petition, the respondent no. 1 Asmoon is the driver of the offending vehicle; the respondent no.2 Lal Bahadur is the registered owner of the offending SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 16:32:12 +0530 Date: 2025.05.03 MACT No. 577/2021 Date of Award:
03.05.2025 vehicle; the respondent no.3 Basir was stated to be the possessory owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent no.4 United India Insurance Company Limited is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Vide order dated 27.02.2022 passed by the Ld. Predecessor, the respondent no.3, who was stated to be the person, who purportedly got the possession of offending vehicle through affidavit, was directed to be dropped from the array of respondents.
Hence, the insurance company i.e. United India Insurance Company Limited is treated as respondent no.3 in the present matter.
3. In its response/reply filed by the insurance company, it is stated inter alia
that the vehicle was being driven in contravention with the terms and conditions of the insurance policy at the time of accident; that there was head on collusion with another truck bearing registration no. DL1LT2063 which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner; that there is contributory negligence of drivers of both the vehicles involved in the accident; that the truck bearing no. HR69A 8665 was duly insured with the answering respondent vide insurance policy, which was valid for the period w.e.f. 05.03.2019 to 04.03.2020, however, the liability, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy and the petitioner is not entitled for the claimed compensation amount as the same bears no relevance to the loss suffered by the petitioner on account of the alleged mishap.
4.
No reply was filed on behalf of respondent no. 1 and 2 and they were proceeded ex parte vide order dated 27.07.2022 passed by the Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal.

I have heard arguments and gone through the record carefully and my issue wise findings are as under :
ISSUE No.1 1.
Whether the petitioner Aliyas suffered injuries in a vehicular accident that took place on 20.01.2020 at about 11 AM at Village Chhapli Ghata, PS Dewair, Rajasthan involving truck bearing registration no. HR69A8665 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no.1/Asmoon in a rash and negligent manner, owned by respondent no.2 Lal Bahadur and insured with United India Insurance Company Limited? OPP 9.
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the SACHIN
Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.05.03 16:32:28 +0530 MACT No. 577/2021 Date of Award: 03.05.2025
Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
10.
SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 16:32:43 +0530 Date: 2025.05.03
However, he neither appeared SACHIN
Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.05.03 16:32:49 +0530 MACT No. 577/2021 Date of Award: 03.05.2025 nor entered into witness box during the course of inquiry.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v.
Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION
OF COMPENSATION
17. The scope of compensation in injury cases has been SACHIN

opennyai_summary.facts:
From the careful perusal of the testimony of the injured / PW-1 including his cross examination, there is nothing material has been elicited to disbelieve the version of accident as given by PW-1.
Rather evidence of PW-1 remained consistent on the aspect of accident, having been caused by rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 (driver of offending vehicle).
Plea of the insurance company that there was contributory negligence on the part of the injured (driver of another vehicle bearing registration DL1LT2063), has not been substantiated by any cogent evidence.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely against respondent no.1.
There is no possibility of false implication of respondent no. 1 and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner herein.
There was an implicit duty on the respondent no.1 to see that his driving did not endanger the life of any other user of the road.
He has failed to exercise the caution incumbent upon him and has clearly neglected his duty of circumspection.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him for not entering into the witness box, to the effect that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
18. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.
The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b),
(iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
19.
23. Admittedly, there is no document placed on record by the petitioner in support of his alleged employment and monthly income.
Thus, for want of cogent and definite evidence being led by petitioner with regard to his actual monthly income, this Tribunal assesses the income of the injured to be at parity with minimum wages of unskilled person in the State of Delhi which at the time of accident i.e. 20.01.2020 was Rs.14,842/- per month.
Thus, he would have taken special rich protein diet for his speedy recovery and would have also incurred some amount towards conveyance charges while commuting to the concerned hospital as OPD patient for his regular checkup and follow up during the period of his medical treatment.
Hon'ble Delhi High Court in the matter titled as "Vinod Kumar Bitoo Vs. Roshni & Ors." passed in appeal bearing no. MAC.APP 518/2010 decided on 05.07.12, has held as under:-
"It is difficult to measure the pain and suffering in terms of money which is suffered by a victim on account of serious injuries caused to him in a motor vehicle accident.
Ld. Counsel for the insurance company has sought to avoid the liability of insurance company on the ground that the respondent no.1 was not having a valid driving license at the time of accident, thus,
there was fundamental breach of the terms and conditions of insurance policy on the part of insured and insurance company is entitled to recovery rights as against the respondent no.1 and respondent no.2 (driver and registered owner of offending vehicle).
32.
It clearly shows that as per the reply of driver of the offending vehicle (respondent no.1) to the notice U/s 134 M.V. Act served upon him by the IO, he has furnished the copy of his driving license to the IO.
Meaning thereby the respondent no.1 was having a driving license at the time of accident, which is further substantiated by the fact that IO has not invoked Section 3/181 M.V. Act in the charge-sheet filed by him against the accused(respondent no.1 herein).
Since, it is an admitted case of the respondent No. 3 /
Insurance Company that the aforesaid vehicle No. HR69A 8665 (offending vehicle) was duly insured with it, therefore, respondent No. 3 / Insurance Co. is liable to pay the amount of compensation to the petitioner / claimant.
opennyai_summary.issue:
15. Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that he had sustained injuries in road accident which took place on 20.01.2020 at about 11 AM at Village Chhapli Ghata, PS Dewair, Rajasthan due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
16.
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.
Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
Now the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
